rapport_notes: Calvin is friendly, helpful, and patient; he spells out the pricing clearly and works through logistics collaboratively with Madeline.
process_discipline_notes: After asking 'Does that all make sense?' Calvin does not hold silence—he immediately re-pitches with 'Cool, well as far as total time...' instead of waiting for Madeline to respond organically.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: MISSING — Calvin jumps directly into logistics ('Did, did you have someone submitted in the system') with no framing of time or benefit promise.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing: 'Any, anything in particular you're concerned about as far as the move goes or any items that you have. We do wrap everything but just want to check-in advance.' This came after 10+ turns of logistics detail (addresses, items, boxes, floors, unload location).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'No, nothing is super sensitive or diverse sentimental'—a clear closure. Calvin does not dig further; he pivots straight to pricing ('Okay, cool well for a move, yeah, for a move like this...').
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 2 (after estimate): 'our no worries damage coverage is also included in the rate, it's just higher evaluation for your items. We allocate up to $2,000 per move.' Valid placement because customer's Stage 1 concern-response was simply 'no' with no expansion.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Covered in Stage 2 (after estimate): 'all of our movers are background check they are trained in-house, they're not contracted labors...They're actually all on our on our website with their pictures and their BIOS.' Valid placement for same reason.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 2: 'we do have an on time guarantee if we're late to a window of arrival we give you we do discount your money back.'
evidence_quotes.communication: NOT COVERED — No mention of day-before call, named crew lead, inbox updates, or any proactive communication touchpoint.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial — gives time range ('a one bedroom apartment typically takes about two and a half three and a half hours') and personalizes slightly ('based on what we're moving at each location'), but the personalization is generic relative to the specific multi-stop complexity Madeline described.
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: 'once we exceed the minimum. We just bill in fifteen minute increments, until the move is completed. So you will just pay for the time that you use that day pass the minimum.'
evidence_quotes.close_rate_lock: MISSING — No mention of rate lock at booking.
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: MISSING — Calvin asks 'Did you want to get on the calendar for that last spot we have on Saturday morning?' but this is phrased as a yes/no confirmation of interest, not a formal 'would you like our help with your move' or equivalent ask. Madeline responds affirmatively, but the ask was transactional/confirmatory, not the full close frame.

top_strength: Calvin handles logistics with precision and clarity—he captures addresses, items, floor details, and sequences them correctly, then delivers a transparent pricing explanation (hourly rate, minimum, 15-minute increments, all-inclusive fees, cost range) that Madeline understands immediately.
coaching_note: Build the call with a quid-pro-quo frame at the top ('Let me ask you a few quick questions so I can get you an accurate quote—should take about five minutes'), ask their agenda before diving into logistics, and add communication differentiators (day-before call, named crew lead) to the takeaway, since you didn't hit them organically in Stage 1.
